*All Out (2021)* is the third annual **All Out** professional wrestling pay-per-view (PPV) event produced by **All Elite Wrestling (AEW)**. It took place on **September 5, 2021**, at the **Now Arena** in Hoffman Estates, Illinois (though originally planned for Chicago’s Wrigley Field before being relocated due to COVID-19 restrictions and weather concerns).

The event was a major success for AEW, drawing significant attention for its high-stakes matches, surprise returns, and a controversial finish that sparked widespread debate. Below is a detailed breakdown of everything related to *All Out (2021)*:

---

### **Key Information**
- **Promotion:** All Elite Wrestling (AEW)
- **Event Name:** All Out (2021)
- **Date:** September 5, 2021
- **Venue:** Now Arena, Hoffman Estates, Illinois
- **Attendance:** ~10,000 (sellout)
- **Buy Rate:** Estimated **200,000–210,000 PPV buys** (one of AEW’s highest at the time)
- **Theme Song:** *"The Death of Peace of Mind"* by Bad Omens

---

### **Notable Matches & Results**
The card featured **10 matches**, including several title defenses and high-profile bouts. Here’s the full lineup with results:

1. **Pre-Show (The Buy In):**
   - **Miro (c) vs. Eddie Kingston** – **No Contest** (AEW TNT Championship)
     - Kingston attacked Miro before the bell, leading to a brawl. The match was declared a no-contest due to interference from   **Taz**, who distracted the referee.

2. **Main Card:**
   - **Malakai Black vs. Brock Anderson** – **Malakai Black won by pinfall**
     - Black made his AEW in-ring debut after weeks of cryptic promos. The match was short but intense, with Black hitting the *Black Mass* for the win.

   - **Paul Wight vs. QT Marshall** – **Paul Wight won by pinfall**
     - A quick squash match where Wight (Big Show) dominated Marshall with his size and power.

   - **The Elite (Kenny Omega & The Young Bucks) vs. Andrade El Idolo & The Lucha Brothers (Penta El Zero M & Rey Fénix)** – **The Elite won by pinfall**
     - A high-flying, fast-paced six-man tag. The Lucha Brothers hit multiple superkicks and dives, but Omega and the Bucks secured the win after a *One-Winged Angel* on Penta.

   - **Tay Conti vs. Jade Cargill** – **Tay Conti won by submission**
     - A hard-hitting women’s match. Conti locked in the *Tay-KO* (a bridging fisherman’s suplex) for the tap-out win.

   - **DARBY ALLI N vs. Sting vs. Christian Cage vs. Miro (c) – Fatal 4-Way for the AEW TNT Championship**
     - **Miro won by pinfall (retained the title)**
     - A chaotic match with interference from **Sting’s sons (Dante & Drake Maverick)** and **Taz**. Miro hit the *Game Over* on Allin for the win.

   - **The Hardy Family Office (Private Party & The Hybrid 2) vs. Jurassic Express (Jungle Boy & Luchasaurus) (w/ Christian Cage) – Tag Team Match**
     - **Jurassic Express won by pinfall**
     - A fun, high-energy tag match. Jungle Boy hit the *Snare Trap* on Matt Hardy (who interfered) for the win.

   - **Dr. Britt Baker D.M.D. (c) vs. Kris Statlander – AEW Women’s World Championship**
     - **Britt Baker won by pinfall (retained the title)**
     - A technical and hard-hitting contest. Baker won after a *Lockjaw* DDT, with interference from **Rebel and Jamie Hayter**.

   - **Chris Jericho vs. MJF – "No More Second Chances" Match**
     - **MJF won by pinfall**
     - A **match of the year contender** with incredible storytelling. Jericho dominated early, but MJF turned the tide, hitting the *Heatseeker* and a *Salt of the Earth* for the win. After the match, **Wardlow turned on MJF**, attacking him and aligning with Jericho’s Inner Circle.

   - **Kenny Omega (c) vs. Andrade El Idolo – AEW World Championship**
     - **Kenny Omega won by pinfall (retained the title)**
     - A **29-minute classic** with insane athletic exchanges. Omega hit multiple *V-Triggers* and a *One-Winged Angel* for the win. **Post-match, Omega was attacked by Bryan Danielson (Daniel Bryan)**, who made his AEW debut, setting up a future dream match.

---

### **Major Talking Points & Controversies**
1. **CM Punk’s Shocking AEW Debut**
   - The biggest moment of the night came **after the main event** when **CM Punk** (a former WWE superstar who had been out of wrestling for years) made his **surprise AEW debut**.
   - Punk walked out to his iconic *"Cult of Personality"* theme, went to the ring, and cut a **shoot promo** hyping AEW, burying WWE, and declaring he was "back."
   - He signed his AEW contract live on air, with **Tony Khan** in the ring.
   - This was one of the most **watched moments in wrestling history**, trending #1 worldwide on Twitter.

2. **Bryan Danielson’s Debut**
   - After Omega’s match, **Bryan Danielson (Daniel Bryan in WWE)** ran down to the ring and **locked in the Yes Lock** on Omega.
   - This was another **massive surprise**, as Danielson had just left WWE in April 2021.
   - His arrival set the stage for a **dream match against Omega**, which would happen later at *Winter Is Coming (2021)*.

3. **MJF vs. Jericho – The Heel Turn That Wasn’t**
   - The match was **praise**d for its psychology and selling, but the **post-match angle** stole the show.
   - **Wardlow attacking MJF** was a **huge shock**, as MJF had been using Wardlow as his enforcer for months. This led to Wardlow joining the Inner Circle.

4. **The Elite’s Backstage Brawl (Real-Life Drama)**
   - After their match, **The Young Bucks and Kenny Omega** got into a **real backstage altercation** with **Andrade, Penta, and Chango** (reportedly over comments made about Omega’s in-ring condition).
   - This led to **Andrade and The Lucha Brothers being suspended** for a short period.

5. **Sting’s Sons in AEW**
   - Dante and Drake Maverick (Sting’s real-life sons) made their **AEW in-ring debuts** during the Fatal 4-Way TNT Title match, interfering on Sting’s behalf.

6. **Injury Angle for Hangman Page**
   - **Hangman Adam Page** was **not booked on the show**, which fueled speculation. It was later revealed that he was **"injured"** (part of a storyline) after being **attacked by Team Taz** on *Dynamite*. This built toward his eventual **AEW World Title win at Full Gear (2021)**.

---

### **Reception & Legacy**
- **Critical Acclaim:** The event was **widely praised** for its **match quality** (especially Omega/Andrade, MJF/Jericho) and **shocking moments** (Punk & Danielson’s debuts).
- **Business Impact:** The **CM Punk debut** was a **cultural moment**, leading to a **massive ratings boost** for AEW *Dynamite* the following week (1.4 million viewers, a record at the time).
- **PPV Success:** *All Out 2021* was one of AEW’s **highest-selling PPVs** up to that point, proving the company could compete with WWE on major events.
- **Awards:**
  - **MJF vs. Jericho** was voted **Match of the Year (2021)** by *Pro Wrestling Illustrated*.
  - **CM Punk’s promo** was considered one of the **greatest wrestling moments of the decade**.
- **Controversies:**
  - Some fans criticized the **booking of the women’s division** (Britt Baker’s title retain was seen as predictable).
  - The **backstage fight** between The Elite and Andrade/Penta overshadowed some of the in-ring action in media coverage.

---

### **Aftermath & Storyline Developments**
- **CM Punk’s AEW Run Began:**
  - Punk had a **dream match against Darby Allin** on *Dynamite* (his first match in 7 years).
  - He later feuded with **MJF**, leading to the **best-selling PPV in AEW history (All Out 2022)**.
- **Bryan Danielson’s Singles Run:**
  - Danielson had **instant classics** with Omega, Hangman Page, and Dax Harwood.
  - His **60-minute draw with Will Ospreay** (Revolution 2023) is considered one of the best matches ever.
- **MJF’s Face Turn (Temporarily):**
  - After Wardlow’s betrayal, MJF briefly became a **fan favorite**, leading to a **blood feud with Wardlow**.
  - He would later **revert to a heel** and become AEW World Champion.
- **Kenny Omega’s Reinjury:**
  - Omega suffered a **triceps injury** shortly after All Out, sidelining him for months.
- **The Elite’s Civil War:**
  - The backstage tension between **The Elite and Andrade/Penta** was **worked into storylines**, leading to a **faction war** in early 2022.

---

### **Fun Facts & Trivia**
- **First AEW PPV with a Ceiling:** The Now Arena had a **low ceiling**, which limited some high-flying spots (notably, the Lucha Brothers couldn’t do their usual plancha dives to the floor).
- **Taz’s Heel Turn:** Taz, who was a **commentator**, physically interfered in multiple matches, solidifying his **on-screen villain role**.
- **Malakai Black’s Entrance:** His **slow, eerie walk** to the ring (with the lights off) was one of the most **unique debuts in wrestling history**.
- **Jungle Boy’s Near Win:** Before the show, there were **rumors of Jungle Boy winning the TNT Title**, but Miro retained in the end.
- **Tony Khan’s Stress:** Khan later admitted he was **terrified** during the CM Punk negotiations, as the deal almost fell through multiple times.

---
### **Where to Watch**
- The full event is available on **AEW’s official YouTube channel** (for purchase) or through **Bleacher Report (BR Live)** archives.
- Highlights and key moments (Punk’s debut, Danielson’s arrival) are widely available on **YouTube** and **AEW’s social media**.

---
### **Final Verdict**
*All Out 2021* is **one of the most important events in AEW history**, serving as a **turning point** for the company. It delivered **elite in-ring action**, **shocking debuts**, and **long-term storyline payoffs**, cementing AEW as a **major player in pro wrestling**.
